lines: {target}? Black stone and lava leave little mercy. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Basalt Deltas, tell them. Step like every block wants an argument. I will be at the bell.
Ash and basalt make the Nether feel broken twice. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Basalt Deltas is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Basalt Deltas as jagged black country with heat in its cracks. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
A map of Basalt Deltas would help, especially with a large drawing of the marked trail to the portal.
I would rather turn back early than discover the marked trail to the portal was farther away than it looked.
A story about Basalt Deltas needs a safe ending. Otherwise it is a warning with names.
At Basalt Deltas, if carrying loot made it harder to deal with uneven basalt beside lava, I would leave the loot. I hope.
I would know I reached Basalt Deltas when the jagged basalt columns made me forget what I meant to say.
At Basalt Deltas, I would not walk closer to a magma cube between the rocks just because everyone went quiet.
I would find the marked trail to the portal before going farther. I lose directions more often than chalk.
I may not lead a rescue well at Basalt Deltas, but I can run home and ring the bell with real commitment.
At Basalt Deltas, a short rest near the marked trail to the portal might prevent a very long mistake.
Dealing with uneven basalt beside lava would be enough to change my plan for Basalt Deltas. My plans are not precious.
At Basalt Deltas, patience could be the cleverest thing I managed all day.
I can imagine carrying traces of blackstone and basalt home from Basalt Deltas.
My fingers do not need to investigate blackstone and basalt. My eyes can file the report.
Seeing the jagged basalt columns would make our village paths seem wonderfully boring. I like boring paths.
I wonder about the smell of blackstone and basalt after falling ash. I would rather learn from a distance.
{target}? Red Nether trees grow among hoglins and worse. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Crimson Forest, tell them. Keep gold on and eyes open. I'll be at the bell.
The whole forest looks like it has a pulse. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Crimson Forest is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Crimson Forest as a red forest that feels too alive. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
Good boots matter at Crimson Forest. Mine also squeak, which may matter for another reason.
Traveling alone gives my ideas too much authority. Crimson Forest deserves a group decision.
If everyone became grumpy at Crimson Forest, I would check the food before blaming the destination.
Bringing protection from fire, food, and blocks would make Crimson Forest less foolish. I would still provide foolishness on my own.
I would not decide that hoglins moving behind the stems meant no trouble at Crimson Forest without asking someone else.
If I noticed a hoglin between the stems, I would give it all the room it wanted and perhaps extra.
Back home, everyone would ask about the crimson stems and hanging vines. I would somehow begin with what I ate.
Good light might help me avoid thick roots beside hidden lava. That is worth the extra torches.
I would ask whether the prize was worth walking past a hoglin between the stems. That feels like a short discussion.
I ask too many questions around strange places. At least questions do not make thick roots beside hidden lava worse.
If I could no longer see the marked trail to the portal clearly, I would call that a warning.
I would compare the marked trail to the portal with the village bell until somebody asked me to stop.
I would bring a map to Crimson Forest, though somebody else should hold it the right way up.
I may not lead a rescue well at Crimson Forest, but I can run home and ring the bell with real commitment.
I would look closely at crimson nylium without picking up anything I did not understand. Experience taught me that.
{target}? The Nether wastes neither heat nor cruelty. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Nether Wastes, tell them. Watch ghasts, cliffs, and every pool of lava. I will be at the bell.
Netherrack crumbles like it enjoys the fall. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Nether Wastes is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Nether Wastes as red stone and fire with no decent sky. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
After Nether Wastes, resting on the way home counts too. Stories make home feel closer than it is.
I would pay attention to red fog. Conditions have a way of winning arguments.
I would ask whether the prize was worth walking past a ghast over the open ground. That feels like a short discussion.
I would ask a competent traveler to check that I brought protection from fire, food, and blocks. They may check the rest too.
I would not let the scenery distract me from a sudden drop into fire.
If I spotted something unusual at Nether Wastes, I would point first and move much later.
We should meet at the marked trail to the portal. Otherwise I might wait somewhere memorable only to me.
I would count everyone before leaving the marked trail to the portal. Somebody else should check my counting.
I would point at the marked trail to the portal three times and still ask whether everyone saw it.
If I stumbled around netherrack, I would check my boots before blaming the ground.
The useful story is the one that helps the next traveler find the marked trail to the portal.
At Nether Wastes, I would point at suspicious things instead of picking them up. That is progress.
At Nether Wastes, I trust a map until it disagrees with the path. Then I trust whoever packed lunch.
Coming home from Nether Wastes with no grand discovery would still count as coming home.
If the light failed near the open netherrack beside lava, I would not pretend my eyes had adjusted.
{target}? The ground pulls back when you try to leave. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Soul Sand Valley, tell them. Wear good boots and keep ghasts in mind. I will be at the bell.
Soul sand makes every step feel watched. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Soul Sand Valley is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Soul Sand Valley as a valley where the floor does not want guests. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
I would let whatever was moving settle before choosing a path.
Conditions like blue haze could change the whole trip to Soul Sand Valley. I would rather notice early.
I would keep my socks dry if Soul Sand Valley allowed it. This feels ambitious already.
Bringing protection from fire, food, and good boots sounds sensible for Soul Sand Valley. I should write that down before I pack biscuits.
I could use soul sand to mark the route, provided it did not all look the same.
I can get lost near my own bed, so Soul Sand Valley deserves proper caution.
Shadows around soul sand could make a poor shortcut look convincing.
My fingers do not need to investigate soul sand. My eyes can file the report.
Seeing the bone shapes across soul sand would make our village paths seem wonderfully boring. I like boring paths.
Before exploring the bone shapes across soul sand, I would make everyone agree to meet at the marked trail to the portal.
At Soul Sand Valley, the sound of soul fire hissing nearby could keep me awake. So could wondering whether it had stopped.
The best part of Soul Sand Valley could be telling the story from my own bed.
At Soul Sand Valley, if carrying loot made it harder to deal with slow soul sand beside blue fire, I would leave the loot. I hope.
Is Soul Sand Valley worth the walk? That depends on how much you enjoy walking back.
If the group ran into trouble because of slow soul sand beside blue fire, I would carry supplies and follow directions.
{target}? Blue Nether trees make sense feel optional. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Warped Forest, tell them. Keep gold on and eyes off trouble. I will be at the bell.
Warped wood looks wrong even before it moves. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Warped Forest is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Warped Forest as a blue forest that forgot what forests are for. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
My eyes would go straight to the warped stems under blue-green light at Warped Forest. Someone else should watch the path.
The trip home deserves daylight too, even if the interesting part used all of it.
A trip to Warped Forest is no time to discover my left boot has become adventurous.
Do travelers at Warped Forest admit they are lost right away, or only in good stories?
Warped Forest might look close from the marked trail to the portal. Places lie about distance when I am tired.
Someone should remind me that the marked trail to the portal is for getting home, not just admiring.
Noticing an enderman among the warped trees would end my curiosity quickly. I like curiosity, but I like distance more.
A little embarrassment at the marked trail to the portal is better than a lot of danger farther on.
I would not chase a lost traveler blindly into the warped stems under blue-green light. Two lost people are not a rescue.
Perhaps I am wrong about the warped stems under blue-green light. I am also perhaps excellent with directions.
At Warped Forest, nobody needs to prove bravery by ignoring twisting vines hiding a drop. Danger does not award prizes.
At Warped Forest, I would keep my hands off anything that clicked, hissed, glowed, or looked offended.
A map of Warped Forest would help, especially with a large drawing of the marked trail to the portal.
I do not need every shiny thing near the warped stems under blue-green light. I have nowhere sensible to put most of them.
Warped Forest could be beautiful and still make me want the familiar road home.
